tasks.short: Adjust digital files to alter print elements, such as fonts, graphics, or color separations.

steps.what: Read the posted change card before this print file.
Draft the fonts, graphics or color separations that fail.
Accept that finding list, or set it aside.
Commit the accepted finding list on this job.
Adjust digital files to alter print elements.

tasks.design: The printing press operator reads the posted change card. A draft in {DOCS} lists the fonts, graphics or color separations that fail a profile, and that draft does not change the customer file. The operator accepts that finding list or sets it aside. A separate commit stores only the list the operator accepted. The operator still adjusts the digital file by hand. Nothing sends the file out of the shop, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The operator hunted through the file for a bad font or a wrong separation, with no posted change to start from.
tasks.enabler_now: When the change card names the element, a profile can list failures and a separate commit can store only the list the operator accepted.
tasks.still_hard: Many cards are free text. The profile must not edit the customer file. The operator still decides the alteration.
tasks.human_edge: Only the operator can see whether a listed failure is the element that should change on this job.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to hunting a bad font. The operator still accepts the list and still alters the file.

reach.task: Treat the finding list as a note, not as a change to the file.
reach.learn: The list is not a change. The operator still alters the file.

evidence.claim: A preflight profile can list file failures such as a missing font, low image resolution, missing bleed, or a wrong color space. The banner time on that page is a different task and is not this saving. This design does not apply automatic edits to the customer file.
Press data that logs output per operator can be used to check performance, and that needs works-council consent first. This finding list is about the file, not a person's output.

assumptions: This task starts when the change card is posted for this file and ends when the operator has altered the file. It does not include booking the order or running the press.

The change card has four fields: job number, file name, element (font, graphic, or color separation), and requested change. The order clerk produces it when the order is booked, and that writing time is theirs. A blank requested change is not a change.

If the card is missing or free text, the read is not shorter and the draft and the commit do not run. A list the operator sets aside is not committed. The draft sits in a scratch area and does not change the customer file. The commit stores only the accepted list, and it is its own step. The operator still alters the file by hand. Nothing sends the file out of the shop, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. Existing document-store runtime is not human effort.
unknowns: What share of change cards name the job, the file, the element and the requested change.
What share of files fail a profile for a reason the card did not name.
research_questions: What share of change cards name the element and the requested change, and how often a profile failure is not the change the card asked for?

already_counted.description: Reading the change card, including a missing card, stays inside the read.
Accepting or setting aside the finding list stays inside that step.
Altering the digital file stays inside that step.

incremental.description: When a profile rule is renamed, the operator checks that the finding list still names a font, a graphic, or a color separation.

approvals.approved_version: the finding list drafted for this file
the finding list the operator accepted for this file

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the change card is missing, so the read is not shorter and the draft and the commit do not run. High is the case where about half the cards are free text, so those two machine steps do not run on that half, and the operator still alters every file. The high is not a vendor hour projection.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct or monitor work of press crews.

steps.what: Read the posted crew card before this shift.
Direct or monitor work of press crews.

tasks.design: The printing press operator reads the posted crew card, then directs and monitors the press crew in the room. That talk stays with colleagues inside the shop. Nothing sends a record, commits a score, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. The design does not log output per operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: The crew list was a verbal handover, with no posted card of who is on the press.
tasks.enabler_now: A posted card names the press, the crew member, the job and the due time, so the read is shorter when those fields are filled.
tasks.still_hard: Who should do what still depends on the room. Logging output per person would need works-council consent and is not in this design.
tasks.human_edge: Only the operator on the floor can see whether the crew is keeping up with the job in front of them.
tasks.altitude: The week is still directing the crew in the room. The card only shortens the lookup of who is assigned.

reach.task: Take direction on the press during the shift.
reach.learn: The card names who is on the crew. It is not a score of their output.

evidence.claim: Press and finishing data that logs output per operator or shift can be used to check performance, and works-council consent comes first. This design does not log output per operator.
No Annex III area applies unless output records are used to evaluate individual operators, area 4(b). This design does not evaluate operators.
Who does what on a press depends on the room, the job and the people standing there. Model knowledge.

assumptions: This task starts when the crew card is posted for the shift and ends when the operator has directed the crew. It does not include scheduling the jobs.

The crew card has four fields: press, crew member, job number, and due time. The shift supervisor produces it at the start of the shift, and that writing time is theirs. A blank crew member is not an assignment.

If the card is missing, the read is not shorter. Directing and monitoring the crew stay at full time. Nothing sends a record, commits a score, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. The design does not log output per person.
unknowns: What share of shifts have a crew card with press, crew member, job number and due time filled in.
Whether any shop already keeps a counter of sheets per operator next to this card.
research_questions: What share of crew cards name the person and the job, and does any current sheet already count output per operator?

already_counted.description: Reading the crew card, including a missing card, stays inside the read.
Directing and monitoring the crew stays inside that step.

incremental.description: When a crew-card column is renamed, the operator checks that press, crew member, job number and due time still line up.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the crew card is missing, so the read is not shorter. High assumes the card is posted for many but not all shifts, and directing the crew stays at full time. The high is not a vendor hour projection.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Download completed jobs to archive media so that questions can be answered or jobs replicated.

steps.what: Read the posted completion card for this job.
Mark the completed job ready to archive, or hold it.
Load the archive media before the completed job is stored.
Download completed jobs onto the archive media.
Open the copy so questions can be answered or jobs replicated.

tasks.design: The printing press operator reads the completion card, marks the completed job ready or holds it, and loads the archive media. A separate download then stores that ready job onto the media. The operator still opens the copy. Nothing sends the job outside the shop, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Completed files were copied by hand onto whatever media was at the press, with no ready mark.
tasks.enabler_now: When the completion card names the file, a separate download can store the job the operator marked ready.
tasks.still_hard: The media is often a disk the operator loads by hand. Whether the job is finished is still the operator's call. Many cards are free text.
tasks.human_edge: Only the operator knows whether this job is complete enough to archive and whether the opened copy is the one that ran.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to copying a file that is already named. The operator still decides it is ready, still loads the media, and still opens the copy.

reach.task: Open only a job the operator marked ready.
reach.learn: Only a job marked ready is on the archive media.

evidence.claim: A flow can store and retrieve files. The banner time on that page is a different task and is not this saving.
Press and finishing data that logs output per operator or shift can be used to check performance, and works-council consent comes first. This archive is the job file, not output per operator.
No Annex III area applies unless output records are used to evaluate individual operators, area 4(b). This archive does not evaluate operators.

assumptions: This task starts when the run is complete and ends when the operator has opened the archived copy. Posting the completion card is the operator's time on the run, outside this task, and stays full time there.

The completion card has four fields: job number, file name, press, and completion date. The operator produces it when the run ends. A blank file name is not a completed job. The completed job file already exists from the run before anyone marks it ready.

If the card is missing or free text, the read is not shorter and the download does not run. The download is its own step and stores only the job the operator marked ready. Loading the media stays in the room. Nothing sends the job outside the shop, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. The archive is the job file, not output per operator. Existing store runtime is not human effort.
unknowns: What share of completion cards name the job, the file, the press and the date.
What share of archive media is a physical disk the operator must load.
research_questions: What share of completion cards name the file, and what share of archive media is a physical disk rather than a folder?

already_counted.description: Reading the completion card, including a missing card, stays inside the read.
Marking the job ready or holding it stays inside that step.
Loading the archive media stays inside that step.
Opening the archived copy stays inside that step.

incremental.description: When the archive path or the media label changes, the operator checks that the download still lands on the media for this job number.

approvals.approved_version: the completed job the operator marked ready for this job number

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the completion card is missing, so the read is not shorter and the download does not run. High is the case where about half the cards are free text, so the download does not run on that half, and the operator still marks the job, loads the media, and opens the copy. The high is not a vendor hour projection.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Control workflow scheduling or job tracking, using computer database software.

steps.what: Read the posted card of due date, machine and paper.
Draft workflow scheduling from due date, machine and paper.
Accept the scheduling line, or move the job.
Commit the accepted scheduling line on the board.
Send the accepted ticket using the computer database software.
Control workflow scheduling on the floor with the crew.
Commit the accepted job tracking status.

tasks.design: The printing press operator reads the posted card of due date, machine and paper. A draft writes a scheduling line in {WORKFLOW}. The operator accepts that line or moves the job. A commit stores that accepted line on the board. A separate send places that same accepted ticket on the press queue in {OPS_SYSTEM}, which is inside the shop. On the floor the operator still controls the schedule with the crew, and a separate commit stores the status the operator matched to the stack. Nothing sends a ticket to a customer, raises an alert, or fills a sheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: The schedule was retyped from the order onto a board, and the ticket was walked to the press.
tasks.enabler_now: When due date, machine and paper are fields, a draft can propose the line, and a commit and a send can each act only on the line the operator accepted.
tasks.still_hard: Many cards are free text. Floor control does not get shorter because a line was stored. A record of output per operator is out of scope.
tasks.human_edge: Only the operator can match the stack on the floor to the job and can refuse a line the card does not support.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to retyping a schedule line. The operator still accepts the line before it is stored or sent, and still controls the floor with the crew.

reach.task: Read the board as the job's place in the schedule.
reach.learn: The board is the job, not a score of the crew.

evidence.claim: A job ticket goes to the press and status comes back by rules on due date, machine and paper. Model knowledge. This shop's saving is not taken from any vendor hour figure.
A flow can move a job. The banner time on that page is a different task and is not this saving.
A print management system holds job records. The page does not name scheduling, and its hour figure is a vendor projection, not this saving.
Press and finishing data that logs output per operator or shift can be used to check performance, and works-council consent comes first. This status is the job's state, not output per operator.
No Annex III area applies unless output records are used to evaluate individual operators, area 4(b). This design does not evaluate operators.

assumptions: This task starts when the schedule card is posted and ends when the status the operator matched is stored. Directing the crew for the shift is a different task.

The schedule card has five fields: job number, due date, machine, paper, and quantity. The order clerk produces it when the order is accepted, and that writing time is theirs. A blank due date, machine, or paper means the line is not written, the ticket is not sent, and the status is not committed.

If the card is missing or free text, the read is not shorter and the draft, the schedule commit, the ticket send, and the status commit do not run. Those four are separate steps. Each runs only on the version the operator accepted. The ticket is that accepted line, not a new version, and it goes to the press queue inside the shop. Nothing sends a ticket to a customer, raises an alert, or fills a sheet. The status is the job's state, not output per operator. Existing database runtime is not human effort.
unknowns: What share of schedule cards name due date, machine, paper and quantity.
Whether the press queue today is a screen on the press or a paper ticket.
research_questions: What share of schedule cards name due date, machine and paper, and is the press queue a screen or a paper ticket?

already_counted.description: Reading the schedule card, including a missing card, stays inside the read.
Accepting the scheduling line or moving the job stays inside that step.
Controlling the schedule on the floor with the crew stays inside that step.

incremental.description: When a schedule-card field is renamed, the operator checks that due date, machine and paper still feed the line, the ticket and the status.

approvals.approved_version: the scheduling line drafted from due date, machine and paper for this job number
the scheduling line the operator accepted for this job number
the job ticket for the schedule line the operator accepted for this job number
the job tracking status the operator matched to the stack on this job

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the card is never posted, so the read is not shorter and the draft, the schedule commit, the ticket send, and the status commit do not run. High is the case where about half the cards are free text, so those four machine steps do not run on that half, and floor control stays at full time. The high is not a vendor hour projection.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still the file, the crew and the press. Less time goes to hunting a bad font or retyping a schedule line. The operator still alters the file, directs the crew, and accepts a line before it is stored or sent.
reach: A finding list is committed only after the operator accepts it, and the operator still alters the file.
The crew is still directed in the room, and no step scores a person's output.
A ticket goes to the press queue only after the operator accepts that line, and the press is inside the shop.
skills_to_grow: Reject a finding the file on screen does not support.
Refuse a ticket send that the accepted line does not match.
Refuse a record that scores a crew member.
role.ambitious_version: The cards are already posted. The operator still alters the file, directs the crew, and accepts the line before a ticket is sent or a job is stored.
